svg.text: Bioactivation hypothesis and what to test next

g.text: 1. How a cyclic basic amine can turn toxic
In Axiom Bio's predicted data a basic N lowers general_tox (median +0.81 without, −0.64 with one; ρ −0.83). Bioactivation is one way a cyclic amine could do this.
Bioactivation by CYP enzymes: Two reactive intermediates, both able to bind proteins

g.text: Gartisertib inhibits UGT1A1 in human liver only
ALT/AST rises: Hepatocyte injury that bioactivation could explain
and Axiom's LDH readout sees (gartisertib 34th vs tuvusertib 74th
Bilirubin rise (UGT1A1): No readout in Axiom's model; linked to
bioactivation only if M26 forms that way (unproven).
Reactive metabolites: LC-MS/MS trapping and GSH depletion
For the recommended candidates (no basic N is no guarantee)
Generate experimental data in Axiom Bio's hepatocyte systems
Run UGT1A1 and OATP1B1/1B3 assays, gartisertib as reference
Human systems only; rat and dog missed this signal
Burris et al., British Journal of Cancer 2024, 130, 1131–1140
